transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
My sleep is completely off—I either lie awake most of the night or crash at odd hours and still wake up exhausted. It has gotten to the point where I'm just really struggling to get through the day.
Aside from your sleep issues and exhaustion, have you been feeling persistently down, or have you lost interest in the things you normally enjoy doing?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love. I used to organize brunches, plan art weekends, and volunteer with a youth art program, but now all of that just feels pointless and exhausting. I end up just ignoring my friends' texts and staying home.
How long have you been experiencing this loss of interest and feeling that things are pointless?

It's been going on for a little over two years now, starting shortly after a painful breakup and some big fights with my parents. Ever since then, it has been a constant struggle, and I just haven't been able to care about the things I used to love.
During these past two years, have there been any periods lasting longer than two months where you felt like your normal self and your mood recovered?

No, I haven't had any periods that long where my mood recovered. This heavy, hopeless feeling has been pretty constant for the last two years, and the closest I've gotten to "normal" was a brief stretch of about two weeks last fall where my mood felt neutral, but I still didn't feel like my true self.
During these past two years, how has your view of yourself been? Have you been struggling with low self-esteem, feeling like a failure, or blaming yourself for things?

Yes, I've been struggling with that a lot. I constantly replay little mistakes, like missing a work deadline or snapping at my mom, and twist them into proof that I'm a horrible person who ruins everything. It gets so bad sometimes that I honestly feel like everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over these past two years, such as eating much less or much more than usual?

Yes, my appetite has really dropped. Most days I have to force down a protein bar or some toast because I just don’t feel hungry, and I've noticed my clothes are getting looser even though I'm not trying to lose weight.
How much are these feelings affecting your ability to work and manage daily chores—are you still able to get things done with great effort, or have you become completely unable to function?

I am barely scraping by with monumental effort right now. At work, I've gone from being a high performer to barely meeting minimum expectations, missing deadlines and avoiding meetings. At home, I just let basic chores like dishes and laundry pile up until I'm completely overwhelmed.
Have you also been finding it difficult to concentrate, focus on your work, or make everyday decisions lately?

Yes, focusing and making decisions has become a major struggle for me. Sometimes at work I'll just stand by the copier, frozen and staring at nothing, unable to decide what I'm supposed to do next until someone snaps me out of it. It makes everything feel too overwhelming to process, which is why I keep missing deadlines and letting my chores at home pile up.
You mentioned feeling like everyone would be better off if you disappeared. Have you had actual thoughts of harming yourself, or have you made any plans to end your life?

I do have those dark thoughts sometimes where I feel like everyone would be better off if I weren't around. However, I don't have any actual plans or intent to harm myself or end my life. It's just a passive feeling that comes over me when everything gets too heavy.
Have you or those around you noticed that you are moving, speaking, or thinking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, that you feel extremely restless and unable to sit still?

Yes, when I'm really down, even simple things like brushing my teeth feel like I'm moving through molasses. My coworkers have actually started asking if I'm okay because I walk so slowly and take forever to respond during meetings.

Over the past two years, has your depression always been this severe—with the slow movement, weight loss, and thoughts of disappearing—or did it start as a milder, constant low-grade sadness that only recently became this intense?

The severe depression has actually been there for most of the past two years, starting just a few months after my breakup. Even though I tried to distract myself at first by throwing myself into work and social events, the heavy feelings of worthlessness, loss of interest, and exhaustion took over quickly and have stayed severe ever since.
Are you still able to manage your basic personal care, such as showering, dressing, and preparing meals, or has the depression made it nearly impossible to do even these basic daily tasks?

It has become incredibly difficult and overwhelming to keep up with basic tasks. Even simple things like brushing my teeth feel like I'm moving through molasses, and I've stopped cooking entirely, mostly just forcing down a protein bar or some toast. Chores like dishes and laundry just pile up in my apartment because I don't have the energy to face them.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a continuous, severe depressive episode lasting over two years, characterized by a persistent depressed mood, near-complete anhedonia, and severe fatigue. She also exhibits multiple cognitive and somatic symptoms including psychomotor retardation, decreased appetite with weight loss, sleep disturbance, feelings of worthlessness/guilt, passive suicidal ideation, and marked indecisiveness. These symptoms have caused severe functional impairment in her occupational and daily life, meeting the criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
